title: I Got Scammed
author: nemi
lines: Okay, please don't judge me. But tell me I'm not the only person whose common sense completely evaporates the second they want something badly.
Because last year, my favorite band announced a tour. One night in my city. And I treated it like an actual national emergency.
Drop morning at ten a.m., I had three laptops open, counting down the seconds. The clock hits zero, I hit refresh... and boom. Sold out in twelve seconds.
Now, a normal person would just close their laptop, sigh, and move on. But my brain went: 'No. We are going to this concert even if we have to buy tickets in black.'
So I started hunting online. And within thirty minutes, I found this guy on a resale forum claiming his friend canceled and he had two VIP passes.
And look—I wasn't completely reckless, okay? I genuinely thought I was being smart. I went full FBI mode.
I made him send screen recordings of his booking email, bank receipts, account history... and everything matched! I sat back at my desk genuinely thinking, 'Wow, I am actually a genius.'

I was already planning what I was gonna wear. Daydreaming about the front row. And right then, he texts: 'Hey, someone else is offering more. You have five minutes to transfer the cash or they're gone.'
And that five-minute timer completely broke my brain. All my detective logic? Gone. I opened my banking app, typed in three hundred dollars, and hit send.
I texted him: 'Sent! Can you forward the tickets?' ...Two seconds later, a bright red exclamation mark: 'Message failed to send. User not found.'
I refreshed. Blank avatar. Blocked. The post was deleted, the guy was gone, and my bank account was sitting at twelve dollars.
I literally paid three hundred dollars just to get blocked on the internet. ...Moral of the story: if the tickets sell out, just stay home. Please. Don't be like me.
